newsitem.title: UK: UK's B&Q says to create nearly 2,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: UK's B&Q says to create nearly 2,000 jobs.

text.p: British do-it-yourself chain B&Q said it is to create almost 2,000 jobs at five new warehouses around the country.

B&Q, which is part of the Kingfisher Group, is planning to open warehouses in Coventry, Wallasey in Merseyside, Bury in Greater Manchester, Stockton-on-Tees in Cleveland, and north London. Each will employ up to 250 people.

A B&Q spokeswoman said the jobs boost was occurring at a time when the housing market and commercial building trade were improving strongly. But she said increasing the number of stores was not reliant on the housing market picking up.
B&Q will launch a recruitment drive early in the new year for 1,800 new posts - half of them part-time positions.

Most of the jobs will be created in B&Q's new warehouse outlets which serve the building trade as well as the public. The remainder will be in its traditional DIY stores. Older people are set to benefit from the company's policy of actively recruiting people aged over 50.
